key_features.classic_presentation: Acute gastritis presents with epigastric discomfort, burning, nausea, and sometimes vomiting. Often associated with NSAID use, alcohol, or stress. Symptoms develop over hours to days. Diffuse epigastric tenderness.
key_features.typical_demographics: All ages. Common triggers: NSAIDs, alcohol, H. pylori infection, stress.
key_features.pathophysiology_brief: Mucosal inflammation from NSAIDs, alcohol, H. pylori, or stress disrupts protective barrier.

diagnostic_questions.context: Epigastric location, often diffuse rather than point tenderness.
Recent NSAID or alcohol use strongly suggests gastritis.
Acute onset over hours to 1-2 days after trigger.

differential_diagnosis.key_difference: More severe, chronic/recurrent, specific meal pattern

red_flags.action: May be ulcer or other serious condition

typical_management: Stop NSAIDs/alcohol, PPI or H2-blocker, bland diet. Usually resolves in few days.
disposition: Outpatient management unless severe or bleeding.
patient_education: Gastritis is stomach lining inflammation. Avoid NSAIDs and alcohol. Medications reduce acid. Most cases resolve quickly with treatment.
